title: Alias templates
recap: An alias template maps template arguments to an existing type expression. Instantiating the alias does not create a distinct type or new data storage.
Forward the intended type arguments instead of accidentally fixing them. A type-identity test can catch an alias that looks generic but always selects one concrete type.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Fix the ScorePair<T> alias so it preserves T instead of always selecting Pair<int>. Then implement maxScore<T>(pair), returning the larger stored value as T (first on equality). The alias names an existing specialization; it does not define a new struct. Both integer and double scores are tested.
expectedOutput: ScorePair<double> must be the same type as Pair<double>
hints: Replace the fixed int in the alias with T.
Compare the two stored values directly.
Do not cast double scores to int.
